integrations.ocrDesc: This is completely optional. Our OCR pipeline extracts document fields using fast heuristics. When you provide an LLM key, it acts as a second-pass fallback, only called for fields where heuristic confidence is below 60%. This can improve accuracy on unusual layouts or poor-quality scans, but most documents process fine without it. Your key is encrypted at rest and only used during your verifications.
integrations.phoneDesc: Optional. Add your own Twilio or Vonage credentials to enable phone number verification as an additional step in your verification flow. Credentials are encrypted at rest.
integrations.amlDesc: Screen extracted names against OFAC, EU, UN, and other sanctions lists on every verification. Matches above the threshold are routed to manual review or hard rejection.
integrations.dupDesc: Detect when the same government ID or face appears in multiple verification sessions. Uses perceptual hashing for documents and locality-sensitive hashing for faces. All hashes are one-way — they cannot reconstruct the original data.
integrations.voiceDesc: Optional speaker verification step. When enabled, users must complete a random digit voice challenge after face matching. Uses 512-dimensional speaker embeddings for voice biometric comparison.

api.quickStartLead: The verification flow is a 5-call sequence. Every processing step is asynchronous: submit, then poll GET /api/v2/verify/:id/status until the relevant field appears.
api.authLead: Every API request must include your API key in the X-API-Key header. You can generate keys in the Developer Portal.
api.sandboxTip: Use a sandbox key during development. Sandbox mode is a property of the key (set in the Developer Portal), not a prefix distinction — all keys use the ik_ prefix. Sandbox uses the same OCR and face-matching pipeline, but counts against a separate quota and does not affect production metrics.
api.flowLead: Each verification is a session with a unique ID. Steps must be completed in order, and each step unlocks the next. Heavy processing (OCR, cross-validation, liveness) is asynchronous: submit the data, then poll GET /api/v2/verify/:id/status to check progress.
api.step1Desc: Creates a new verification session for a user. Returns a verification_id that ties together all subsequent uploads and results. One session equals one complete identity check.
api.fieldUserIdDesc: Your unique identifier for the user being verified.
api.fieldSandboxDesc: Set true to use sandbox mode. Defaults to false.
api.fieldAddonsDesc: Optional add-on features to enable for this session.
api.fieldAmlDesc: Enable AML/sanctions screening against OFAC, EU and UN lists. PEP screening is also available via AML_PROVIDER=pep. Runs automatically after identity verification completes.
api.step2DescAfter: of the identity document (passport, driver's license, national ID). OCR extraction and image quality analysis (Gate 1) run during upload. The response includes
api.step2DescEnd: with extracted fields and confidence scores. If the image quality is too poor, the session is hard-rejected.
api.fieldDocumentDesc: JPEG, PNG, WebP, or PDF. Max 10 MB.
api.step2CalloutBefore: If Gate 1 rejects the document (blur, low resolution), the session status becomes
api.step2CalloutMiddle: and subsequent steps will return 409. Check
api.step2CalloutEnd: for guidance to display to the user.

api.step3DescMiddle: — it unlocks live capture. If the front and back do not match the same document, the verification immediately moves to
api.fieldDocTypeStep3Desc: Must match the document_type used in Step 2.
api.fieldDocumentBackDesc: JPEG, PNG, or WebP. Max 10 MB. Field name is 'document'.
api.step3CalloutBefore: Cross-validation now auto-triggers during back-document upload. Poll
api.step3CalloutEnd: , cross-validation did not pass — do not proceed to live capture. Check
api.step4DescBefore: One endpoint, two gates, two liveness modes. Submit a
api.step4DescMid3: checks that the image is from a live person, then
api.step4DescEnd: auto-triggers to compare against the document photo (128-d cosine similarity, threshold 0.60).
api.passiveDesc: Just upload the image — no extra data needed. 8 heuristic signals (entropy, pixel variance, EXIF, file size, etc.).
api.headTurnDesc: Client captures 5–12 timed frames while the user turns their head. Server runs face detection plus 7 weighted checks. Pass ≥ 0.70. Zero ML on the client.
api.clientPassiveBrowser: None — just upload the image file
api.clientHeadTurnDeps: None — all face analysis runs server-side
api.step4TipStrong: Head turn needs zero ML dependencies on the client.
api.step4TipBodyBefore: Just capture JPEG frames from the camera using standard browser APIs (
api.step4TipBodyAfter: ). The server handles all face detection and yaw estimation. This is what the hosted verification page and demo use internally.
api.fieldSelfieDesc: JPEG or PNG image captured live from the user's camera via getUserMedia(). Max 10 MB. Static file uploads will fail liveness.
api.fieldLivenessMetadataDesc: JSON-stringified challenge data for head_turn liveness. Omit for passive mode (lowest pass rate).
api.step4WarningStrong: The selfie must be a live camera capture, not a file upload.
api.step4WarningMid: The liveness engine runs anti-spoofing checks on every image — even in passive mode (8 heuristic signals including EXIF analysis, compression artifacts, moire detection). A static photo uploaded from disk will almost certainly fail with
api.step4WarningMid2: because it lacks camera metadata and has re-compression artifacts. Always use
api.step4WarningEnd: to capture directly from the device camera.
api.step4ChoiceBody: For low-risk flows (e.g. sandbox, basic onboarding), passive is fine. For all production identity verification, use
api.step4ChoiceEnd: — it provides strong anti-spoofing with zero client-side ML dependencies.
api.step4MetadataWarnMid: is provided but fails validation (wrong schema, missing fields), the API returns
api.step4MetadataWarnEnd: code. It does not silently fall back to passive mode. Always check that your metadata format matches the schema above.
api.step5Desc: The single source of truth for a verification session. Use this endpoint for polling at each processing stage and for reading the final result. Returns the full record including OCR data, cross-validation scores, liveness score, and face match score.
api.pollingNext3: check final_result; if not "failed", proceed to Step 4
api.crossValidationDesc: Retrieve the cached cross-validation results separately. Cross-validation runs automatically during the back document upload (Step 3), so this endpoint is only needed if you want to query the results independently.

api.selfieDescEnd: (never 403), so the endpoint can't be used to enumerate other developers' verification IDs. Returns only the selfie URL — no OCR, PII, or other documents.

credentialVerify.description: Paste any Identity Verification JWT-VC to verify its authenticity. Signature verification happens entirely in your browser — no API key needed.
